FOR codex/counterpart-diagnostic -- RED AT outboard, rc=11 after 363 s, main unchanged at 20c0cd375. ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is one flag.

WHAT FAILED. Not the 55 python tests -- those passed ("Ran 55 tests ... OK"). What failed is validate_sample in tools/digest/experiments/the-counterpart/run.py:170, on the base arm:

    dossier/base/metadata-base.json
    command: cargo metadata --locked --offline --format-version 1 --manifest-path tools/digest/Cargo.toml
    exit_code: 101, direct_child_waited: True
    stderr: error: failed to download `windows-link v0.2.1`
            Caused by: attempting to make an HTTP request, but --offline was specified

WHY. `windows-link` is a target-gated Windows crate. It is in tools/digest/Cargo.lock, and `cargo metadata` resolves the FULL dependency graph for every target, so it wants the crate file even though nothing on a Linux box ever builds it. lefford has never downloaded it -- its registry cache holds zero windows-link entries -- and a normal `cargo build` here never would. So `--offline` fails on a crate the platform will never compile.

THIS IS HOST-DEPENDENT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KNOWING. On a box whose registry happens to be warm for that crate the identical run goes green. It is not a race and not main: `codex/federation-next`, your own ancestor, passed all four stage phases twenty minutes earlier at 1196 s, so the cause is inside your four extra commits -- 2715e5ca2 is the one that exercises this arm.

FIXES, YOURS TO CHOOSE. Drop `--offline` for the metadata call; or pre-fetch (`cargo fetch --manifest-path tools/digest/Cargo.toml`) before the arm and keep the flag as a guarantee about the SAMPLE rather than about resolution; or pin the metadata call to the host platform if the full-graph resolve is not what the assay needs.

ONE OBSERVATION ABOUT THE DIAGNOSTIC ITSELF, offered because it cost me the first five minutes. `raise ValueError('failed command or uncollected child')` covers two independent conditions -- `exit_code != 0` and `direct_child_waited is not True` -- and the message does not say which fired. Here it was purely the first: the child was collected correctly, waited True. A reader of the log alone would reasonably start hunting a process-reaping bug that does not exist. Splitting that into two messages is a two-line change and would have named the cause in the log without anyone opening the dossier.

THE DOSSIER SURVIVED and is worth reading before you rerun: /home/nathan/.local/state/hornvale/counterpart-unreserved.1ffoIB/dossier -- 18 samples, 17 clean, the one failure isolated in base/metadata-base.json with full stderr, timing and RSS.
